_note: State overrides. Every constant not listed here is taken from data/constants.json unchanged: hot water demand, efficiencies, COP, installed costs (DCCEEW RIS Table 20 is national), rebate (0) and deal parameters. The efficiencies are the NSW climate zone (Zone 3) values; they have not been adjusted for this state's climate.
name: Tasmania

EF_electricity_kgCO2e_per_kWh.source: DCCEEW, 'Australian National Greenhouse Accounts Factors 2026', Table 1, 'Tasmania': scope 2 = 0.23, scope 3 = 0.03.
EF_electricity_kgCO2e_per_kWh.check: Read from the official XLSX (archived copy, captured 2026-09-10, text dump in data/source_text/national-greenhouse-accounts-factors-2026.xlsx.txt).

emissions._gas_not_modelled: Table 6 gives 'C' instead of a value for Tasmania's scope 3 natural gas factor, so no upstream gas factor is published, and no residential gas standing or regulated offer covering postcode 7000 appears in the CDR data. Gas hot water is therefore not priced for Tasmania.

tariffs.electricityPlan: Aurora Energy Residential Peak and Off-Peak (regulated offer)
tariffs.timeOfUse: Two rates: peak $0.32898/kWh weekdays 07:00 to 09:59 and 16:00 to 20:59, off-peak $0.154727/kWh at all other times. At 03:00 the off-peak rate applies. The plan has no controlled load circuit.
tariffs.retailer: Aurora Energy's REGULATED offer is Tasmania's regulated reference offer.
tariffs.source: AER Consumer Data Right, Energy Product Reference Data API, postcode 7000. Raw responses in data/cdr_raw/tas/ (scripts/fetch_cdr_states.py).
tariffs.heatPumpRate: The heat pump is priced at the rate in force at 03:00 on a weekday, the overnight window a timer targets, as in NSW and Victoria (src/lib/cdr.ts).
tariffs.gst: CDR unit prices are stored the same way for every state, so all states are on the same basis.
